title: Pediatric neurologist visit
what: The doctor checks how your child's nervous system, movement and speech are developing. The exam is calm and painless.
why: For routine checks in the first year and before nursery or school; for delayed development, headaches, seizures, tics or poor sleep.
duration: the visit usually takes 20 to 40 minutes, with the report right after
tell_doctor: How the pregnancy and birth went
When your child began to hold up the head, sit, walk and talk
What exactly worries you and for how long
If there have been seizures, head injuries or fainting

prepare.title: Observations
prepare.text: Write down what worries you. If it happens in episodes, record a video.

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: Choose a time when your child is usually alert, not hungry and not sleepy.

prepare.title: For a baby
prepare.text: Bring a favorite toy, water and a snack.

bring: Your child's ID and your ID
The medical record or discharge summaries
Results of earlier tests, if any
Videos of episodes or movements, if you recorded them
steps: The doctor asks you about development and complaints
Watches how your child moves, plays and reacts to sounds and objects
Checks reflexes with a small hammer
The doctor explains the conclusion and, if needed, orders tests
feel: The exam is not painful - reflexes are checked with light tapping
A baby may cry at the unfamiliar place - this does not stop the doctor
after: The doctor gives advice or a referral for tests
Do not stop prescribed medicines on your own
Come back for a follow-up when the doctor sets it
red_flags: Seizures, loss of consciousness, sudden drowsiness or vomiting after a blow to the head - call your local emergency number

faq.q: Should we go to a neurologist if the child is healthy?
faq.a: Yes, routine checks in the first year are needed to notice any delay in time.

faq.q: What if my child cries through the whole visit?
faq.a: It is fine. The doctor is used to it and can still examine your child.

reminders.text: Pediatric neurologist tomorrow. Take your child's medical record and a toy, and write down what worries you.
